data.summary: Microscopist on 4 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 7 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors

observations.finding: DAPI (blue) nuclei markedly enlarged in all 4 treated fields vs DMSO control f_b165a4caad77, which shows uniform oval ~38-39um long axis nuclei. Treated show many 1.2-1.3x longer and >1.5x area, with increased fraction of very large nuclei.
Whole cell bodies markedly enlarged and spread, with more cell-free black background at 24h. Peripheral spreading increases with dose. DMSO confluent monolayer vs treated dispersed.

Nuclei shape irregular; decreased circularity. Increased binucleation / bilobed closely apposed double nuclei per cell most obvious in central cluster f_717863296525 and f_10c6bfbe2dcc, also in f_e1b9ff7c6d87 center and f_9b1232e520b6. Lobed/multinucleated not seen in DMSO.
DAPI integrated brightness higher in enlarged nuclei, consistent with increased DNA content / polyploidy. Not uniformly brighter, but large/bilobed nuclei often paler blue and larger.

beta-tubulin (green) filamentous network retained, not depolymerized or bundled. Fibers extend to periphery scaled to larger cell size, no obvious monopolar/multipolar spindles or tubulin clumping. Sparse bright yellow mitotic-like cells in both DMSO and treated, no mitotic arrest burst.

F-actin (red) cortical and cell-cell contact staining retained, cells remain adherent. No fragmentation, punctate aggregates, or collapse to foci. Cell shape change is spreading not rounding/shrinkage. Stress fibers/cortex visible similar to DMSO.

Cell number/density appears lower in treated fields (231-291 cells measured across 2 fields per well) vs dense DMSO field, consistent with cytostatic effect, with dose trend: 10uM fields more sparse than 1uM.

Real-lab orthogonal validation (e.g., phospho-histone H3/DNA-content cytokinesis assays) would be needed for mechanistic proof beyond imaging.

reflection.text:
Unblinding: AZ-A, BBBC021 internal code with no curated structure/mechanism in PubChem/ChEMBL (e13), truth MoA Aurora kinase inhibitors. Conclusion Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.84 (e12) was correct (verdict correct: true).

What the evidence got right and why:
- The core discriminating phenotype was reproduced in 4 independent wells spanning 0.01 to 10 uM, all replicate 1 but with 184-327 cells each: frac_large_nucleus z +24.2 to +30.9, nuc_area z +17.2 to +20.0, cell_area z +17.4 to +26.5, with integrated DNA content increased (e2, e3, e4, e7). The lowest dose tested 0.01 uM (w_1ba4909e4e, 184 cells, frac_large_nucleus z=+30.9) was already maximal, indicating highly potent polyploidy induction. This saturated polyploidy across 4 doses is what we weighted in update_hypotheses (e11) and submit_conclusion rationale.
- Visual phenotype (e5) on 4 fields: lower density vs DMSO, 7 observations, candidate Aurora kinase inhibitors, specifically describing large/bilobed/binucleate nuclei with intact filamentous tubulin and actin. Combined with dose_response e10 frac_mitotic_like constant across acquired wells, this excluded Eg5 inhibitors, microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers and actin disruptors which require monopolar spindles, mitotic arrest, or cytoskeletal collapse - correctly contradicted in e11 (p 0.01 for Eg5, microtubule, actin classes).
- compare_to_reference_atlas (e6) gave 6/10 Aurora kinase inhibitors top neighbors, 2/10 DNA replication, 2/10 DNA damage. Literature found in run supports this morphology: Aurora B inhibitor AZD1152-HQPA/barasertib is documented to induce polyploidy and cytokinesis failure PMID 25752998, with related AZD1152 Aurora B inhibition phenotypes PMID 28639950 PMID 20175926 PMID 21222513 PMID 39799765. lookup_compound for barasertib (e16) as Aurora-B inhibitor provided a class match control, while etoposide (e17) DNA topoisomerase II inhibitor framed the DNA damage alternative.

What was ambiguous/misleading and what we missed:
- e6 was not decisive: mean similarities were very close (Aurora vs DNA replication/DNA damage overlap) and 4/10 neighbors were non-Aurora. This overlap is biologically expected because DNA replication stress and DNA damage also increase nuclear size/DNA content. Our p=0.84 correctly retained ~0.11 combined for DNA replication (0.06) + DNA damage (0.05) but the review was right to flag residual plausibility.
- Dose-response was easy to misread: frac_large_nucleus Spearman rho -0.80 p=0.2 (e8) and nuc_area rho +0.40 p=0.6 (e9) are flat/non-significant with only 4 points. Because we started at 0.1 uM then 1 uM and 10 uM and finally 0.01 uM, every well was already saturated, so no EC50/onset could be resolved within the 0.01-30 uM available range (e1: 8 doses 0.01-30 uM, 4 of 4 wells left). Flat trend is therefore expected for potent Aurora inhibition, not contradictory, but without a sub-0.01 uM or DMSO acquired well we could not demonstrate dose-dependency directly.
- Acquisition choice: list_available_experiments -> acquire_well mid, high, low, lowest was well chosen to span onset-to-maximum, but all acquisitions were rep 1. Large effect sizes z>17 make replicate failure unlikely, but we left formal replicate reproducibility untested and exhausted budget 0/4 leaving no room for orthogonal analysis of acquired wells.

Why p=0.84 calibration was appropriate: huge, reproducible binucleation/failed-cytokinesis without mitotic arrest and intact cytoskeleton is specific for Aurora B among large-nucleus inducers, but the atlas similarity tie and saturated dose-response without sub-threshold anchor justified staying below certainty. As proposed, real-lab follow-up would be p-Histone H3 S10 immunofluorescence + Hoechst integrated intensity DNA content vs DMSO and barasertib control plus live-cell time-lapse for failed cytokinesis/endoreduplication to mechanistically separate Aurora from DNA-related polyploidy.
